**6B.10 Research Note: Narendra Modi in 2024**

**Bottom line**
The evidence is mixed and leans slightly negative on the specific question of whether ordinary people ended 2024 with clearly better life chances than they entered it with. There is real evidence of stronger macro management, some pro-poor program design, and expanded service delivery infrastructure. But the strongest counterevidence is lived-condition evidence: jobs, inflation, food prices, rural distress, and school-meal cutbacks kept biting ordinary households, while some spending was openly shaped by coalition and vote-retention politics.

**Accepted Claims**
- **India enters 2024 with strong headline growth momentum** | Publisher: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation / PIB | Date: 31 May 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2022323&lang=2&reg=3 | Summary: The government reported 8.2% real GDP growth in FY 2023-24 and 7.8% in Q4, meaning Modi began 2024 with favorable macro conditions and some room to improve life chances. This supports a constrained positive reading, though it is still macro output rather than direct welfare outcomes. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.9
- **Interim budget avoided a giveaway and prioritized disadvantaged groups** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 1 Feb 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-finance-minister-unveils-budget-with-focus-on-poor-women-youth-and-farmers/1948406/ | Summary: Reuters reported that the budget explicitly centered the poor, women, youth, and farmers while resisting a classic pre-poll giveaway. That is good evidence that the government was at least trying to route growth toward ordinary households rather than pure short-term patronage. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **Fiscal discipline preserved room for longer-term public investment** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 1 Feb 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/economy/india-refrains-from-populist-budget-before-election-trims-fiscal-deficit/1948823/ | Summary: Reuters said the administration kept fiscal consolidation and avoided a big election splurge. This matters for life chances because it preserved policy space for future services and investment, although it does not itself prove those benefits reached ordinary people. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.9
- **Technocratic fiscal rule-setting remained in place** | Publisher: Reuters via Investing.com | Date: 30 Jan 2024 | URL: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/indian-government-appoints-members-for-new-finance-panel-3287402 | Summary: Reuters reported the government appointed experienced officials and economists to the Finance Commission. That supports the view that economic rule-setting still had some professional discipline, which is a precondition for improving ordinary people’s prospects over time. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.9
- **Rural-income and non-farm job targets signaled a broader livelihood agenda** | Publisher: Reuters via The Straits Times | Date: 8 May 2024 | URL: https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/indias-modi-chasing-reform-legacy-shifts-income-goals-for-struggling-farmers | Summary: Reuters reported targets to lift rural incomes, expand non-farm jobs, and increase agricultural investment. This is direct positive evidence that the government was not only managing aggregate GDP, but also aiming at ordinary people’s earning power and livelihood mobility. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.9
- **Post-election budget redirected spending toward jobs and rural programs** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 23 Jul 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/india-focuses-on-job-creation-rural-areas-in-first-budget-after-election/2186863/ | Summary: Reuters reported that the first post-election budget kept jobs and rural spending high, along with higher education loans and manufacturing incentives. That is real positive evidence for life chances, but it was also reactive to electoral pressure rather than clearly programmatic alone. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.9
- **Budget shifted toward investment-linked spending while holding the deficit down** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 23 Jul 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/india-budget-shifts-spending-priorities-while-keeping-fiscal-deficit-in-check/2187377/ | Summary: Reuters said the budget cut the deficit target to 4.9% of GDP while raising capital and investment-linked spending. This is the strongest evidence that Modi’s government tried to leave behind a stronger economic platform for ordinary people, though the gains are indirect and long-run. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.9
- **Health and education-related human-capital measures expanded** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare | Date: 28 Sep 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressNoteDetails.aspx?ModuleId=3&NoteId=153215&lang=1&reg=3 | Summary: The government highlighted expanded Ayushman Bharat coverage for seniors, U-WIN, new medical seats, and digital health registries. If these measures stick, they improve ordinary people’s long-run life chances through health access and human-capital formation. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.9
- **ABDM expanded standardized health infrastructure** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Health and Family Welfare | Date: 17 Dec 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2085201&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: The government said ABDM had built large-scale digital health infrastructure, including ABHA accounts and linked records. This supports a positive reading on durable access and continuity of care, although the evidence is official self-reporting. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.9
- **Digital Agriculture Mission improved data-driven support for farmers** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare | Date: 2 Sep 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2050966&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: The mission used digital public infrastructure, crop estimation, and data-driven support for farmers. This is evidence of a more capable state apparatus that could improve rural livelihoods over time, though again it is official self-reporting. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.9
- **Rural women’s self-help groups expanded at scale** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Rural Development | Date: 30 Jul 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2039162&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: DAY-NRLM reportedly mobilized more than 10 crore rural women into self-help groups. That is meaningful evidence of broadening women’s economic inclusion, especially for poorer households. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.9
- **Housing support adapted to regional cost differences** | Publisher: Press Information Bureau / Ministry of Rural Development | Date: 9 Aug 2024 | URL: https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2043919&lang=2&reg=48 | Summary: The Cabinet extended PMAY-G with different unit assistance for hill and northeastern states. This is a real access measure that better matches support to need, which improves the odds that poor households can actually use the program. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.9
- **Women’s ownership was emphasized in rural housing and work programs** | Publisher: PTI via ThePrint | Date: 31 Dec 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/women-empowerment-remained-in-focus-for-rural-development-ministry-in-2024/2425889/ | Summary: The ministry said over half of MGNREGS beneficiaries were women and PMAY-G ownership strongly favored women. This is positive evidence for gendered life chances and asset-building, though it remains official/programmatic reporting. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.9
- **Budget spending also reflected coalition bargaining and voter retention** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 23 Jul 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-spends-billions-on-jobs-key-allies-in-first-budget-after-election/2187546/ | Summary: Reuters reported that more than $5 billion went to coalition-led states and that the budget was explicitly aimed at winning back voters and retaining support. That weakens the claim that improvements in life chances were being allocated neutrally or primarily by need. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.9
- **Coalition partners pressed for funds and cabinet jobs** | Publisher: Reuters via Investing.com | Date: 6 Jun 2024 | URL: https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/modis-appeal-clouded-in-india-election-by-prices-jobs-graft-survey-says-3472931 | Summary: Regional allies demanded more funds and cabinet positions as coalition talks began. This is evidence of patronage-heavy bargaining at the center of government formation, which cuts against a clean “ordinary people first” story. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.9
- **Rural voters still felt jobs and inflation pressure** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 7 Jun 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/rural-vote-fall-cost-indias-modi-a-decisive-election-win/2121496/ | Summary: Reuters reported that BJP losses in rural constituencies were driven by lack of jobs and high inflation. This is direct counterevidence that ordinary people had clearly better life chances by 2024. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **Voter distress centered on prices, jobs, and falling incomes** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 6 Jun 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/modis-appeal-clouded-in-india-election-by-prices-jobs-graft-survey-says/2119215/ | Summary: The reporting linked support erosion to household distress. This undercuts a strong claim that Modi left ordinary people materially better off in lived terms, even if the macro picture looked stronger. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **Food inflation cut into school meals for poor children** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 11 Oct 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-high-food-inflation-leaves-less-in-lunch-boxes-of-poor-school-children/2307077/ | Summary: Reuters reported that school meal budgets had not kept pace with inflation, forcing cutbacks in nutrition for poor children. This is strong counterevidence because it shows basic life chances for vulnerable children were not fully protected. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.8
- **Inflation remained a live constraint despite disinflation progress** | Publisher: Reserve Bank of India | Date: 8 Aug 2024 | URL: https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=58448 | Summary: The RBI said growth was strong and inflation broadly declining, but it also stressed stubborn food inflation and external risks. This supports a constrained reading: Modi inherited some positive macro momentum, but ordinary people still faced meaningful cost-of-living pressure. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.9
- **Household distress and inflation still shaped the election outcome** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 23 Jul 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-faces-delicate-balancing-act-in-post-election-budget/2186495/ | Summary: Reuters described the post-election budget as balancing fiscal prudence with voter anger and coalition demands. That suggests the government had not yet translated macro strength into broadly felt life-chance gains and was still responding to distress. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.8, 6B.9
- **Communal scapegoating and hate speech weakened equal civic standing** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint; Human Rights Watch | Date: 23 Apr 2024; 14 Aug 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-calls-rivals-pro-muslim-as-election-campaign-changes-tack/2053223/ ; https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/14/india-hate-speech-fueled-modis-election-campaign | Summary: Modi’s “infiltrators” rhetoric and HRW’s reporting on hate speech show a campaign environment that marginalized minorities rather than clearly expanding ordinary people’s dignity and opportunity. This does not prove life chances worsened for everyone, but it is strong negative context. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.8
- **Manipur and J&K show severe protection failures** | Publisher: Human Rights Watch; Amnesty International; Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 11 Jan 2024; 16 Jul 2024; 10 Sep 2024; 31 Jul 2024 | URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/india-increased-abuses-against-minorities-critics ; https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/india-authorities-missing-in-action-amid-ongoing-violence-and-impunity-in-manipur-state-new-testimonies/ ; https://theprint.in/india/internet-suspended-in-parts-of-indias-manipur-as-students-clash-with-police/2261451/ ; https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/31/india-repression-persists-jammu-and-kashmir | Summary: These sources describe deaths, displacement, internet shutdowns, curfews, detentions, and weak accountability. This is direct counterevidence to a broad claim that ordinary people were left with better life chances overall, because safety and basic functioning are prerequisites for opportunity. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.8
- **Political finance remained opaque and capture-prone** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint | Date: 16 Feb 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/explainer-what-were-indias-electoral-bonds-and-how-did-they-power-modis-party/1969006/ | Summary: Reuters described the electoral-bonds system as enabling unlimited anonymous donations and noted that the BJP was the biggest beneficiary. This is counterevidence because opaque political finance usually correlates with patronage, not broadly shared opportunity. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.7, 6B.9
- **State communication and monitoring space were still politicized** | Publisher: Reuters via ThePrint; Election Commission of India via Hindustan Times; Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | Date: 21 Mar 2024; 17 Jun 2024 | URL: https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-puts-on-hold-unit-for-fact-checking-online-content-about-govt/2009612/ ; https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/election-commission-to-it-ministry-stop-sending-viksit-bharat-messages-on-whatsapp-101711006490551.html ; https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/india | Summary: The government created a fact-checking unit to police online content about itself, the Election Commission had to stop government-branded WhatsApp outreach, and Reuters Institute flagged broad regulatory pressure on press freedom. That weakens the case that the state was building a neutral environment that would reliably improve ordinary people’s future prospects. | Question IDs: 6B.10, 6B.9, 6B.8

**Search Gap**
- The evidence base is strongest on macro performance, budget design, and service-delivery infrastructure, but much weaker on direct longitudinal proof that ordinary people’s actual life chances improved in 2024.
- I did not find a clean independent study of income mobility, learning outcomes, health outcomes, or earnings trajectories for 2024 that isolates Modi’s effect from baseline growth and inflation.
- Positive evidence is often official self-reporting or policy design; negative evidence is often lived-condition reporting. That means the best-supported conclusion is cautious: some foundations improved, but ordinary people did not clearly and uniformly end 2024 with better life chances than they inherited.
